recipes.name: Rock's T-Bone Steaks
ingredients_raw: 0.75 teaspoon garlic powder, or to taste
0.75 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
0.75 teaspoon ground coriander, or to taste
0.75 teaspoon ground turmeric, or to taste
4 (16 ounce) t-bone steaks, at room temperature

steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Stir together salt, paprika, black pepper, onion powder, garlic powder, cayenne pepper, coriander, and turmeric in a small bowl.
Rub seasoning over steaks on all sides.

Cook steaks on the preheated grill to the desired degree of doneness, 3 to 3 1/2 minutes per side for medium-rare. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of each steak should read 130 degrees F (54 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Rock's T-Bone Steaks
raw_recipe.description: Grill a T-bone steak with a simple blend of seasonings, including paprika, garlic, coriander, and turmeric, to make it taste fantastic and flavorful.

review.reviewBody: We've tried this steak rub three times now, and tonight was the best.... the first couple of times I used the full amount of salt, and tonight I cut both the salt and turmeric in half. Be sure to apply the rub just before grilling. If you leave it on too long, the flavor gets too strong, and the meat loses it's juice. Thanks, Rocky... the best steak we've had all year!

I followed someone else’s recommendations and used half the salt. I also didn’t have ground coriander or tumeric, so I left it out. After cooking it I melted butter on top. It was SOOOOO GOOD!! Husband approved! Cooked for 12 minutes in an air fryer. Perfect!

This was amazing as is. I did omit half the amount of salt because it seemed a bit excessive (and that's that I like salt). Also, I seared it in a cast iron pan with a bit of butter, garlic, and thyme. Wow! My fiance loved it! Definitely going to make again!

This was awesome! I did as others suggested by halving the salt and sprinkling the spices onto the meat just before cooking the T-bones. The spices complimented the meat and I was really surprised at how well the tumeric added to the overall flavour. It was delicious. I'll probably use this spice mix again with T-bone.

I used 3 T-Bone steaks (on sale at Kroger this week). Brushed with Olive Oil and sprinkled with Savory Sensation (Homemade Gourmet spice).
Cooked over High Heat for 8 min total. Medium (some pieces had more red than others)

Delicious!

Love love love! Everyone at the cookout got to try a bite and everyone loved it! I took a bowl and poured canola oil into it then added all the seasonings. I covered each T-Bone, then put the steaks into ziploc bags. Since it made it a marinade, I poured it over the steaks and then marinated for about 8 hours. The oil definitely helped to keep the seasonings on the steak when I put them on the grill.

Did as other reviewers and cut the salt in half. Used the rub on two occasions already. Plenty salty for me! May be a little spicy for some (cayenne pepper) but right up my ally. Cooked my T-Bones in the air flyer. Came out great! Would follow this recipe (sans salt) for rub again without hesitation.

Forgot to mention what I added to your recipe rock. 1st, I cut the amounts for 1 steak. I coated both side with olive oil, and sprinkled 1 1/2 caps full o liquid smoke. Then I added 1/2 tsp of rosemary, 1/2 tsp of basil. Rubbed all the ingredients in on both sides and let it stand for 30 minidress after I pulled it from the feeding.
Husband loved it! I only used 1/2 t. Salt.

I looked at all the reviews and also noticed for the first time that you can change the amount of servings you have and calculate accordingly. I had two servings.. I didn't have Turmeric either like most of us, but it was still good. Since I HATE anything spicy hot, I only used a pinch of cayenne. One thing I added which Emeril suggested on his recipe for T-bone Steaks was to put 1 Tbsp of Olive oil on each side of each steak before rubbing the spices in, which was an awesome idea. I used a little less pepper like everyone suggested. And I did add an additional sprinkle of Emerils original spices on both sides before grilling. And for a good size steak, really make sure your grill is super hot and set a timer for 3.5 minutes on each side. It was a very great steak and will be using this recipe again!!

I made this rub for two steaks. I followed the recipe except for adding salt and turmeric, didn't have any, but used ginger instead.
Only thing is we had an unexpected situation and had to put the steaks in a ziplock with the rub on them and didn't cook them until the next day. I was so afraid that sitting that long would be too much spice. But..Oh my gosh...were they ever good! Not too much and you could still taste the juicy steak. Thanks Rocky...we'll be using this again.

This is my favorite rub for all my beef, but especially my T-bones. I have made this rub about 15x now and it still amazes my family that it is so good. The only changes I make is by using smoked paprika (1:1 ratio) because that was the only kind of paprika I have in the house 100% of the time and I now omit the cayenne pepper, because I am a wuss. My boys put the cayenne on once the steaks hit their own plate. I have not made this with regular paprika, but now I have Hungarian Sweet Paprika in the house and we are going to experiment with that and use some Aleppo Pepper tonight. Wish me luck!
Gotta make twice as much next time.
Easy to mix up and makes all steaks taste great but use less on thinner steak cuts. It is best on tbone as recipe states
Followed this recipe. Steaks had a great flavor
I used smoked paprika instead. That was the only change I’ve done. I would scale back a little on the salt next time, though. I applied the rub right before grilling.
Bern my go to for years, first meal I feed my wife when we were dating.
It takes a little longer than 3-3/12 minutes per side for a good medium steak. I grilled mine 5-5/12 minutes with an internal temp of 150F
I was really excited for to make this seasoning for steaks-for some reason I did not care for it. :( The flavor did not work for me. :/ Thank you for the recipe!! :)

Very good, the seasonings were incredible, they didn't overpower the steak and accented it quite well. The cooking process was fun, but martians attacked me while preparing for the steak and I woke up 13 minutes later on the kitchen floor and martians eating my steak.
